title: Unit 3 : Session 6 : SLO 2 — Carry-Save Adders
sections: Answer: b) To add three or more binary numbers by separating the sum and carry bits.
It is called carry-save addition because the carry bits are not propagated immediately to the next more significant bit; they are 'saved' and computed separately from the sum bits.
Each stage takes three input bits and produces a sum bit and a carry-out bit, avoiding the delay of waiting for a carry to ripple through the adder.
Step 1 — Generate the partial products of the 4-bit multiplication.
Step 2 — First CSA stage: take three partial products and add them with a layer of carry-save adders, producing a sum vector and a carry vector.
Step 3 — Subsequent CSA stages: feed the previous sum and carry vectors plus the next partial product into another CSA layer; repeat until only two vectors (one sum, one carry) remain.
Step 4 — Final addition: add the final sum and carry vectors with a conventional carry-propagate adder (ripple-carry or carry-lookahead) to obtain the product.
With traditional ripple-carry adders, every addition has a delay proportional to the number of bits because the carry ripples from LSB to MSB, and these delays accumulate over multiple additions.
A carry-save adder tree adds three numbers in constant time regardless of bit-width, because carries are not propagated; the single carry-propagate addition happens only once at the very end.

Key advantage: a significant speed improvement — the expensive carry propagation is postponed to one final step, making carry-save addition much faster for multi-operand scenarios such as multiplication.
